target_customer: Long-term care and other healthcare facilities that need per diem staff, and the workers who fill shifts
problem: Facilities scramble to cover open shifts through expensive agencies, while workers lack flexible, reliable shift access.
business_model: Two sided shift marketplace taking a margin on each filled shift

founders.name: Wei Deng
founders.background_notes: YC page lists experience in law, finance, product and operations. YC blog describes the company as a pivot.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile marketplace with matching, credential checks and payments. Hard parts were operational, not technical.

defensibility.rationale: Local density of workers and facilities helps, but several per diem staffing apps exist and facilities multi-home.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent is recorded as copying or buying it. Traditional staffing agencies and rivals such as ShiftKey, CareRev and IntelyCare remain competitors.

market_need_then: Facilities relied on agencies for per diem shifts. No dated 2016 or 2017 demand data was found, only the later company description.

branding.domain_note: Moved from clipboardhealth.com to clipboardworks.com and now clipboard.com (clipboardworks.com redirects, 301, to clipboard.com).

rebrands.why: One profile site dates the shift to 2024; not confirmed by an official announcement

brand_strength.rationale: Large worker base and a profitable marketplace with 11M shifts covered, but the generic word name and no evidence of a brand led growth story.

pivots.from: Earlier product (YC blog says the company pivoted)
pivots.why: YC blog headline describes pivoting to a billion dollar idea; details not read

outcome_analysis: Clipboard pivoted into healthcare shift staffing, raised a 50 million Series B and a 30 million Series C at 1.3 billion post-money in 2022, and says it has been profitable since 2022 with over 1,000 staff. The main open risk is worker classification litigation, including a 2025 settlement near 6 million dollars and a pending 2026 case against a rival.
notes: Series B date conflicts (January, March or June 2021 across sources). Profitability and 1.3B valuation claims come from the company's own careers page. Lawsuit details come from a single outlet. The company website in the data was a careers page that redirects. No competitor sources dated near 2016 or 2017 were found.
